title: Replace global mutexes with latchless session-fence + compact KV rehydration to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Multiple production incidents and long-running tail latency traces point to global mutex contention in the continuous-batcher pipeline and an expensive KV rehydration path when shards migrate or snapshots are reloaded. This ticket reduces tail latencies by: 1) introducing a latchless session-fence primitive to replace the current global mutex used by slot allocation and batch commit; 2) implementing compact, incremental KV rehydration that avoids full snapshot deserialization on common hot paths; and 3) decoupling scheduler heartbeat work from admission critical-path to prevent stalls under bursty ingress.
Goals:
- Cut 95th/99th percentile latency on small token requests by at least 20%
- Reduce observed pause events caused by global mutexes
- Keep functional correctness: no regressions in KV consistency across shard handoffs
Scope:
- Design and implement session-fence (lock-free linearizable marker per session)
- Replace two hotspots in batch coordinator using session-fence (slot allocation and commit barrier)
- Add a streaming KV rehydration API that can apply snapshot deltas while allowing reads to continue
- Add a lightweight background compactor that trims rehydration footprints and bounds memory growth
- Update admission and scheduler pipeline so heartbeat and metric aggregation are async and retryable
- Add unit, integration, and perf tests with synthetic and real trace workloads
Rollout plan:
- RFC + design doc review with infra and storage teams
- Implement feature-flagged changes behind runtime flag "latchless_session_fence" and "incremental_kv_rehydrate"
- Canary on low-traffic region for 48h, monitor latency/failure metrics
- Gradual ramp with automatic rollback on regression
Criteria for Done:
- All new code behind flags and tests pass in CI
- Bench: 95th latency improved >= 20% on representative load
- No KV-consistency regressions in chaos tests (shard handoff + priming)
- Design doc and post-mortem published
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Kaur: Created ticket after post-incident review (2026-02-07). Root cause summary attached in Confluence. Marking as P1 due to customer-facing tail latency spikes.
2026-02-12 Miguel Ortega: Spike day — prototyped an epoch-based fence (non-blocking) in a toy harness. Observed no throughput regression on microbench but still need to validate in end-to-end traces.
2026-02-18 Infrastructure sync: Decided to decouple heartbeat work from admission. Ops requested a new metric 'session_fence_backpressure' for heartbeat lag.
2026-02-25 Design review: Storage team asked for backward-compatible snapshot format. Agreed on delta-stream with compatibility header. Action: Miguel to add compatibility tests.
2026-03-03 Engineering update: Feature flag scaffolding merged (runtime#4821). Added feature-gate checks in allocator and commit path. Unit tests added for fence state transitions.
2026-03-08 Perf run: 95th latency improved by 18% on synthetic 8-token workload in canary env. 99th improved by 10% — close but short of target. Plan: optimize KV rehydrate hot path next sprint.

2026-03-12 QA note: Ran chaos test with shard handoff and concurrent rehydrate. Observed one read-after-write anomaly in the delta apply path (race in ordering). Blocking until PR with ordering fix is ready.
2026-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Updated estimate: +2 points to address delta ordering bug and add chaos regression test. Will submit fix PR today.
implementation_notes: Prefer atomic ops and sequence numbers over condition variables
Keep feature-flag scaffolding minimal to avoid hot-path branching overhead
Provide metrics to detect fence stalls and delta backlog
